glosses: first/third-person plural subjunctive II of ertrinken

examples.text: Er hat versucht seine Frau im Meer zu ertränken.
examples.translation: Il a essayé de noyer sa femme dans la mer.

examples.text: Hör auf die Pflanze zu gießen, du ertränkst sie ja!
examples.translation: Arrête d’arroser la plante, tu les noies !

glosses: Se noyer, se suicider en se jetant à l’eau.

examples.text:
Nichts sei so schwer zu ertränken wie ein Verdacht, weil nichts so leicht immer wieder auftauche, antwortete er endlich.
Der Kommissär sei unverbesserlich, lachte Hungertobel, der das Ganze als einen harmlosen Spaß ansah.
examples.translation:
(...) après quoi il observa que rien n’était plus difficile à noyer qu’un soupçon. « Il n’existe rien au monde pour revenir aussi facilement et toujours en surface ! »
Sacré commissaire ! Il était décidément incorrigible, s’amusa Hungertobel, qui prenait tout cela pour une simple plaisanterie.

glosses: To die from suffocation while immersed in water or other fluid.

examples.text: When I was a baby, I nearly drowned in the bathtub.
Old woes, not infant sorrows, bear them mild / Continuance tames the one; the other wild, / Like an unpractised swimmer plunging still, / With too much labour drowns for want of skill.

glosses: To kill by suffocating in water or another liquid.

examples.text: The car thief fought with an officer and tried to drown a police dog before being shot while escaping.
The pretty-vaulting sea refused to drown me, / Knowing that thou wouldst have me drown’d on shore, / With tears as salt as sea, through thy unkindness:

glosses: To be flooded: to be inundated with or submerged in (literally) water or (figuratively) other things; to be overwhelmed.

examples.text: We are drowning in information but starving for wisdom.

One could almost drown surveying the ways different eras have honored her in painting, sculpture, icons, architecture, music and poetry; venerated her with titles, liturgies, prayers and feasts; and taught about her in spiritual writings, theology and official doctrine.

glosses: To obscure, particularly amid an overwhelming volume of other items.

examples.text: The answers intelligence services seek are often drowned in the flood of information they can now gather.
